So I can’t actually produce the image bytes via the Google endpoint you’ve currently got wired up.

- “A cute smiling teapot (ceramic, slightly chubby, with a friendly face) doing a kickflip on a skateboard mid-air, dynamic pose, little motion lines, cartoon illustration, bright cheerful colours, clean thick outlines, soft shading, white studio background, high detail, crisp, centered composition.”

2) **If you want me to generate the image here**, I need you to enable/expose an image-capable model in this project so it appears in `ListModels` (or tell me the exact model name that *does* appear for you).  
If you paste the relevant model name you see in your own `ListModels` output (the one that supports image generation), I’ll immediately re-run the request and return the image.

<Current Time: 2026-02-07 16:19:35 Saturday afternoon>
It doesnt mention 2.0 at all? Are you looking at the live version?

You are right to challenge that, Sir: I cannot guarantee I’m seeing the *current live* content of that page from here, because I’m not browsing it interactively in this chat.

What I *can* say with certainty is:

- In this environment, I attempted to call `models/gemini-2.0-flash-exp-image-generation:generateContent` because that has been the commonly documented Gemini image-generation model name on Google’s Gemini API docs in the recent past.
- The API here returned **404 NOT_FOUND**, and when I list available models I do **not** see any `*-image-generation` model at all.

So, either:
- the docs have since been updated to a different model name (very plausible), or
- the doc is showing a capability that isn’t enabled/available for the API project backing this tool.

If you paste the **exact model name** the doc currently shows (the bit after `models/…`) or the relevant snippet from the page, I’ll use that model name verbatim and try again.

<Current Time: 2026-02-07 16:20:45 Saturday afternoon>

- When I run the **Brave Search skill**, it runs a local script from your repo (typically under `~/projects/jevons/skills/brave-search/`).

So I’m not talking about your whole machine in general, nor your browser; I mean the specific local code + filesystem context the assistant’s tool runner is operating inside.
